author: claude-mentor-session
claim: A diagnosis control is only valid on the metric that defines the failure: for routed-SHAPE failures, point-to-polyline deviation discriminates (control h7 median 4px/max 14px vs failing h11/h16 max 41-42px) while aligned-support deltas do not (h7 +0.067/+0.119 overlaps h11 +0.096/+0.079), so a support-delta control 'confirms' false mechanisms for shape claims.

measurement.command: python3 probe: load pair-matrix-v6/TowneLake-full.json legs for holes 11/16/7, compute min point-to-segment distance from each routed cell (x*field.scale) to the registered truth polyline (y-viewport.top); compare vs the external session's support-delta table
measurement.numbers: shape deviation median/p90/max px: h11 10/40/42, h16 10/33/41, h7 control 4/10/14; closest approach to bend vertex: 45/45/10px vs W/2=18.5; support deltas (non-discriminating): h11 +0.096/+0.079, h16 +0.017/+0.003, h7 +0.067/+0.119

control: h7, TowneLake's other bent hole: hugs its bend on the shape metric (median 4px) while showing support deltas in the same range as the failing holes — the metric that separates failing from working cases is shape, not support
frames: truth: full-capture px minus viewport.top -> cropped px; routed legs: field cells x field.scale -> cropped px
risk: Deviation thresholds are course-zoom-relative (W/2=18.5 at dev zoom); on a 2x capture the same slack doubles in px. Also assumes registered bend vertices are accurate to ~a few px (TowneLake registration quality 1.2-1.5px median on endpoints; bend vertices unaudited).
history: Arose from correcting CX-060: an external session ran a control but compared on support deltas, so the control 'confirmed' a false one-mechanism story; the owner's one-line challenge forced the shape measurement that overturned it.
